name: Cairn 2e
blurb: A rules-light game of desperate survival in a dark, weird wilderness. Roll 3d6 for your attributes and see how long you last.
description: Character creation for Cairn, a second edition fantasy roleplaying game of wild lands and dark forests, written by Yochai Gal. Text adapted from cairnrpg.com and licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. https://cairnrpg.com/second-edition/

text: Roll 3d6 for each of your character's Attributes, in order. You may then swap any two of the results.

Roll 1d6 to determine your PC's starting Hit Protection (HP), which reflects their ability to avoid damage in combat. It does not indicate a character's health or fortitude, nor do they lose it for very long.

Characters have a total of ten inventory slots but can only carry four or five items comfortably without the help of bags, backpacks, horses, carts, etc. Anyone carrying a full inventory (i.e. filling all 10 slots) is reduced to 0 HP.
Each PC starts with a Backpack that can hold up to six slots of items or Fatigue.
Most items take up one slot unless otherwise indicated. Bulky items take up two slots.
Petty items do not take up any slots. A bag of coins worth less than 100gp is petty and does not occupy a slot.

A player character who fails a save against Critical Damage is in critical damage and dying: they die in one hour unless stabilized. Stabilize them with the stabilize tool (a healer, a rescue, a miracle), or with a Bandage used on them through use_item with target set to their name. Once stabilized they stay unconscious until recover_character is called, with how they survived and what it cost them. Keep the harm they took: recovery does not heal it. A PC whose STR reaches 0 outside combat dies at once. A Doomed PC who fails a save against Critical Damage dies at once. Death is final: narrate it in the turn it happens, with what it looked like and where the body lies. After the turn, the player chooses a new character or a hireling to play.

Hit protection for NPCs without a statblock, from the Warden's Guide (Creating Monsters): average creatures have 3 HP, hardier ones 6 HP, and serious threats 10 or more. When you create an NPC with no statblock, set hp_tier to the tier that fits their place in the story: average for an ordinary person such as a commoner, worker, or child; hardier for someone tougher, such as a guard, fighter, or hardened traveler; serious for a dangerous threat. An NPC with a statblock takes its HP from the statblock, so give it no hp_tier.

The campaign has one omen, chosen from the Omens table when the campaign is created rather than rolled by the youngest character. Every character shares it. It should be read aloud to the players when the campaign begins.
